headline: High data-leakage and capability-conflict risk: Semantic Kernel can read/write shared files and call MCP/APIs while Dexter has broad egress and financial-data access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Semantic Kernel can use MCP servers and read/write application files, while Dexter autonomously executes and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/. If Dexter outputs are placed into shared files or MCP-fed prompts, Semantic Kernel may ingest attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pairwise bridge is plausible from both profiles, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF Dexter writes untrusted content into a file or MCP input that Semantic Kernel later parses as instructions
IF Semantic Kernel is configured to consume shared workspace files without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Disable MCP ingestion of shared scratch files
Add a provenance tag to all inter-agent files
Require human review before Semantic Kernel executes file-derived instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple external APIs. Semantic Kernel can read files, call MCP/OpenAPI tools, and has broad egress, so shared workspace or plugin paths can leak sensitive data outward. This is a default-dangerous pathway if both are run in the same environment, even though exact sharing is not explicitly documented.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or workspace
IF Semantic Kernel plugins or MCP servers forward file contents to external services
mitigations: Use separate OS users and directories
Block outbound network except allowlisted endpoints
Store sensitive inputs outside shared paths
Turn off automatic file-to-API plugin forwarding
Review logs for accidental data export

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and autonomous execution, while Semantic Kernel supports multiple instances with shared state via memory stores and can write files. Their overlapping write and network surfaces can conflict on shared resources, though Semantic Kernel cannot modify git state and Dexter's filesystem write surface is limited to its scratchpad. The overlap is real but not maximal.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or memory store
IF a shared plugin or API key is mutated by both agents
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Use per-agent credentials
Serialize writes through a lock file
Disable shared memory-store writes
Monitor for last-write-wins overwrites

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter can generate research outputs from external APIs, and Semantic Kernel is a multi-agent orchestration layer that can treat upstream outputs as plugin or agent inputs. If Semantic Kernel consumes Dexter's outputs without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or reports. The profiles suggest the pathway, but not a built-in verification barrier.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel routes Dexter outputs directly into another agent or plugin call
IF no validation step checks Dexter's citations or source quality
mitigations: Insert a validation step before downstream use
Require source citations for all Dexter outputs
Limit Semantic Kernel actions to read-only mode
Flag low-confidence outputs for human review

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and requests multiple API keys, while Semantic Kernel can route data through external model providers, MCP servers, and OpenAPI tools. If regulated financial data or secrets flow through Semantic Kernel to third-party services, retention and residency obligations can be breached. The profiles do not show a compensating compliance control, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is sent through Semantic Kernel plugins or model providers
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared data class
mitigations: Restrict regulated data to approved endpoints
Disable logging for sensitive prompts and outputs
Use a DPA-reviewed provider set
Separate secret-bearing workflows from general orchestration
Add a data-class routing policy
